newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Feb loses despite weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, Feb loses despite weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Monday in a moderate session, with February pressured most of the day by technical selling despite Arctic cold weather and reports of firmer cash, sources said.
February closed down 6.2 cents at $3.254 per million British thermal units. March settled 1.1 cents higher at $2.86. Most others ended off slightly.

"Regardless of the thermometer, I think the rally is over. I'm expecting some downward pressure soon, it's just a matter of time," said one Texas-based producer, noting storage in the critical consuming areas was in pretty good shape.
Traders said an early rally attempt on the cold stalled early, triggering a flood of technical selling and long liquidation.

While chartists noted near support held today, leaving prices stuck in the recent range, most agreed the failure to gain ground in the face of the season's coldest weather could be an ominous sign for the bulls.
Below-normal temperatures are forecast for most of the nation this week, though Texas temps are expected to moderate somewhat.

Technically, they still pegged February support in the remaining gap between $3.11 and $3.19, with better buying likely in the $2.60s. Resistance was seen in the $3.80-3.84 area and then at $3.96. The contract high is $4.02.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed Monday by five to 10 cents to the mid-to-high $3.90s. Midcon pipes slipped almost 50 cents to the $4.30s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 0.9 cent to $2.396. NYMEX said an estimated 33,479 Hub contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 48,794.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Monday.

On the KCBT, February closed down 7.1 cents at $3.06, while deferred months finished two to 10 cents lower. The East/West spread widened by 0.9 cent to 19.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 215 contracts traded, up slightly from Friday's total of 200.

Separately, ANR said cold weather in the U.S. Gulf cut about 200 mmcfd of natgas out of 1.2-1.3 bcfd on the southeast leg of its pipeline system. Other pipelines reported only minimal impact from well freeze-offs.
